subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: For Codex-backed WebChat sends, should `chat.send` continue to return `started` before native thread startup/turn-start is proven, or should Codex fail fast or force-rotate before ACK when the native thread may be unrunnable?
rationale: Current code has partial mitigations, but the remaining boundary is a user-visible API/liveness contract rather than a single mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Prove Before ACK
options.body: Require Codex startup and a safe `turn/start` path, or a forced fresh-thread rotation, before returning `started` for WebChat sends.

options.title: Keep Immediate ACK With Recovery
options.body: Keep non-blocking ACKs but add visible post-ACK error, audit, and recovery paths that prove no user message is silently lost.

options.title: Close As Mitigated
options.body: Treat the current overflow/startup guardrails as sufficient only after a live or fixture replay proves this exact wedge no longer reproduces.

recommendation.title: Prove Before ACK
recommendation.body: Require Codex startup and a safe `turn/start` path, or a forced fresh-thread rotation, before returning `started` for WebChat sends.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged PR #88207 owns the current native-thread overflow rotation behavior that most directly intersects the reported wedge.
